title: PhishTriage report
description: The JSON report of PhishTriage (phishtriage analyze --json). Every value from an email is defanged and your own addresses are REDACTED, as in every other report format; a script that needs live values must refang them itself, on purpose. Non-ASCII characters are written as \uXXXX escapes.

schema_version.description: Changes when this schema changes in a way that breaks readers

defanged.description: Always true: no value in the report is live

tool.description: The tool that wrote the report

generated_at.description: When the report was made, UTC, ISO 8601

scoring_source.description: 'built-in scoring.yaml', or the name of the scoring file given

scoring_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the scoring file: which exact weights made the verdicts, lower-case hex

enriched.description: True when reputation lookups were made (--enrich)

redacted.description: How many pieces of text had one of your addresses removed

files.description: Every file: analysed ones first, in the order given, then those that failed

attack_tag.description: A MITRE ATT&CK technique the evidence points to

id.description: T1566 Phishing; .001 Spearphishing Attachment; .002 Spearphishing Link

reason.description: One signal from scoring.yaml and what it added to the score

signal.description: The signal's name in scoring.yaml (or the rule, for a rule scoring.yaml does not know)

label.description: What the signal means, in plain words

points.description: Points added; 0 if nothing counted, or the signal is worth 0

rules.description: The rules of the findings behind it

note.description: Why it added nothing, e.g. '1 of 92 engines say malicious; 3 needed'; empty when it counted

override.description: True if it made the verdict malicious on its own

score.description: A verdict: one email's, or a whole file's (its worst email)

total.description: The score, 0-100 (100 when an override decided it)

attack.description: ATT&CK techniques; empty for likely benign

basis.description: What the score could use: no lookups, every lookup answered, or some unanswered

unanswered.description: With basis 'partial': lookups that got no answer

reasons.description: What counted first, most points first; then what did not count

answer.description: One line of reputation: a service's answer, a domain's age, or why a value was not looked up

text.description: The line, e.g. 'VirusTotal: 5 of 95 engines: malicious'

skipped.description: This line says why the value was not looked up

answered.description: The service really answered (found, or did not know the value)

ioc.description: An indicator of compromise found in the email

value.description: The value, defanged: hxxps://evil[.]test, evil[.]test, 203[.]0[.]113[.]9, a[@]evil[.]test

seen.description: How many times it is in the email

allowlisted.description: On the allowlist, so not looked up (still listed: allowlisted is not safe)

group.description: URLs: their registered domain, defanged, for grouping; empty for other kinds

looked_up.description: With --enrich: was a lookup planned; null without --enrich

reputation.description: With --enrich: one line per answer; empty without

attachment.description: An attachment (never opened: only its bytes are hashed and its type sniffed)

name.description: The file name the email gives, defanged where it contains a domain

real_type.description: The type found from the content (libmagic); empty if unknown

members.description: The names inside a ZIP archive

encrypted.description: A password-protected ZIP: scanners cannot look inside

reputation.description: With --enrich: the answers for its hash

auth.description: SPF, DKIM and DMARC, from the trusted Authentication-Results header

source.description: Which header the results come from

found.description: False when no trusted header was found: the results are unknown

spf.description: pass, fail, softfail, neutral, none, ... or unknown

compauth.description: Microsoft's own verdict; unknown when its servers wrote none

compauth_reason.description: Microsoft's reason code, e.g. '001'; empty if none

finding.description: What one check found. Findings have no points: scoring.yaml decides what they are worth

facts.description: Numbers and fixed words behind a finding, e.g. {'malicious': 5, 'engines': 95}

email.description: One email: the file itself, or one forwarded inside it

where.description: '' for the file itself; '1' for the first forwarded email; '1 > 2' for the second one inside that

level.description: 0 for the file itself, 1 for an email inside it, 2 inside that, ...

from_address.description: The sender's address, defanged, or REDACTED if it is one of yours

other_from.description: Any further From addresses (a red flag in itself)

subject.description: The subject, with links, addresses, domains and IPs defanged

message_id.description: The Message-ID, defanged: search other mailboxes for it (refang first)

sender_ip.description: The IP the email came from, defanged; empty if no header says

sender_ip_source.description: Which header gave the sender IP

sender_ip_certain.description: False when it came from a Received header, which is easier to fake

forwarded.description: How many emails are forwarded inside this one (each has its own entry)

defects.description: Notes from parsing, e.g. a part that could not be decoded

not_written.description: Checks that are not written yet

name.description: The file name only, without its folder (which would show your user name)

verdict.description: The file's verdict: the worst email in it. null when the file could not be analysed

decided_by.description: '' when the file's own email decides, else the deciding email's 'where'

emails.description: The email, then every email forwarded inside it, in report order

error.description: Why the file could not be analysed; empty when it was
